statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative name certification is valid for 90 days and is not extendable; upon rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of notification, or submit up to five alternative names in a new application; final administrative denial may be challenged before the Audiencia Nacional within two months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as final domicile. A virtual office may serve only as a provisional registered address during incorporation, but the CNMV license for the Multi-Family Office (EAF under Ley 6/2023) requires a permanent physical establishment in Spain with dedicated office space, secure IT and data-protection infrastructure, local staff presence, and accessible compliance records; a purely virtual address constitutes a mandatory ground for regulatory refusal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (60% quantified risk): CNMV and SEPBLAC conduct risk-based on-site inspections of licensed financial advisory entities within the first 18-36 months of operation, with approximately 40% probability of an unannounced physical visit during the first supervisory cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital of EUR 3,000 for an SL, with at least 25% paid up upon incorporation and the balance within five years. Proof of payment must be furnished; no separate escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the proposed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada resolves unanimously: (1) to form the company with share capital of three thousand euros (EUR 3,000) fully subscribed by the initial shareholders; (2) to adopt the registered office at [full address in Spain] for all communications and operations; (3) to appoint [Name1] as Managing Director, [Name2] as Director, and [Name3] as Alternate Director; (4) to designate [Name] as Corporate Secretary; (5) to approve the Articles of Association in final form and authorize their execution and registration with the Registro Mercantil; (6) to empower the directors to complete all filing procedures, pay fees, and obtain tax identification. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; supplementary corporate registration at Registro Mercantil Central for definitive NIF issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a foreign-owned Spain SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada): (1) incorporate before a Spanish notary with bank deposit of minimum capital (€1 for nominal share capital; €3,000 for share-premium rules applicable depending on articles), and the notary requests a provisional corporate NIF from AEAT; (2) after inscription at the Mercantile Registry, the definitive NIF (usually prefixed with an 'X' for an SL with non-resident ownership) is obtained; (3) the SL files Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) within one month of incorporation and before commencing taxable activities; (4) each foreign shareholder without a permanent establishment obtains a non-resident NIF (NIF-N) via Form 030 through a Spanish tax representative with power of attorney; (5) the SL applies for the AEAT electronic certificate to access the Sede Electrónica and the digital signature required for Verifactu-compliant billing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SL is a tax-resident corporation taxed on worldwide income under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) at a headline 25% rate (Art. 4, 7, 10 LIS); newly created SMEs carrying an economic activity may apply a 15% reduced rate for the first two tax periods on the first €300,000 of tax base (Art. 29 LIS). No pass-through or transparent election exists for an SL. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation, mitigated by the participation exemption (Art. 21 LIS) for qualifying foreign-source dividends and capital gains from ≥5% holdings held ≥1 year. The MFO's portfolio-advisory fees are treated as Spanish-source service income subject to IS when the services are performed in Spain, with CFC rules (Art. 100 LIS) applied to any passive income parked in low-tax jurisdictions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Statutory elections include: (i) tax consolidation group regime (Art. 61–69 LIS) for groups directly or indirectly holding ≥75% of the subsidiary's share capital, filed with AEAT by September of the year preceding the first consolidated tax year; (ii) the foreign-source dividend/capital-gain exemption and the ETVE-like substance-safe election (Art. 21 LIS); (iii) the special VAT group regime (Art. 155–162 LIVA) for entities under 100%/≥75% common control enabling single VAT returns; (iv) the cash-accounting special regime for businesses with turnover ≤ €2,000,000; (v) provisional payment options under Art. 40.3 LIS; (vi) anti-hybrid rules (Art. 15bis.h LIS) requiring documentation rather than elective treatment. In the MFO context, discretionary portfolio-management mandates may electively rely on the VAT exemption for fund/capital management services (Art. 20.1.18ª LIVA) by notifying Form 036.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax), governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA), RD 1624/1992, and EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold triggering general VAT registration: any SL conducting an economic activity must be registered in the Censo de Empresarios (Form 036/037) before the first taxable transaction. Optional simplification thresholds exist within an otherwise mandatory filing: simplified special regime for turnover ≤ €250,000 (≤ €125,000 for service activities); agricultural special regime ≤ €75,000; cash-accounting special regime for businesses with turnover and collections ≤ €2,000,000. No corporate de-minimis exemption applies to an MFO.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal control applies through three convergent mandates: (i) Verifactu (RD 1007/2023, effective from 1 July 2025) requires all invoicing software to be AEAT-certified or self-audited and to produce digitally signed invoices with unique QR/stamping identifiers, plus a tamper-evident transaction register transmitted to AEAT; (ii) B2B e-invoicing is mandatory for all professionals under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece'), with interoperable platform standards (Facturae 3.2) and the requirement to deliver electronic invoices through connected exchange platforms; (iii) the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) regime applies only to taxpayers with business volume > €24 million and to VAT groups, mandating near-real-time invoice-level reporting to the AEAT webservice/API within 4 days of issuance and 8 days of receipt. No pre-export fiscal stamp is imposed on standard invoices, but zero-rated export invoices must reference the supporting customs exit declaration code in the electronic VAT ledger.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% effective IVA (exemption with deduction of input VAT) is available for: (i) export of goods to non-EU destinations, provided the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch (Art. 21 LIVA); (ii) intra-EU supplies of goods to VAT-identified counterparties (Art. 25 LIVA), substantiated by the customer's valid intra-community VAT number; (iii) services directly linked to exported goods (transport, handling, ancillary services) under Art. 70 LIVA; (iv) B2B services treated under the place-of-supply rule as supplied outside Spain (Art. 69 LIVA) — for an MFO, discretionary portfolio-advisory and fund-management fees invoiced to a non-EU financial institution or fund domiciled abroad fall outside Spanish IVA upon proof of the customer's foreign establishment; (v) if the MFO is an authorised manager of EU UCITS/AIFs, the Art. 20.1.18ª LIVA exemption applies irrespective of the investor's residence. All zero-rating claims require accounting evidence of the shipment or service export, including the customs declaration reference for goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) — copy carrying the ES customs office code, export procedure, and the electronic exit confirmation from the SAE/CEA system
Commercial Invoice (export invoice) using the applicable VAT exemption code (e.g., E-0 or R-1) and containing sender/consignee identification
Transport document — Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or CMR agreement bearing the AEAT-validated exit stamp or ICS/ECE manifest reference
Proof of physical exit — ICS/ECS 'results of export' message or certificate of origin tied to the customs declaration

Inward Remittance Certificate — SWIFT MT103 or bank credit note evidencing collection of the export proceeds from the foreign buyer; for services exports, the equivalent client payment receipt and the foreign customer's establishment evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retroactively claw back improperly claimed zero-ratings within the four-year statute of limitations by regularisation assessment, plus late-payment interest (approximately 3.75% annually) and collection surcharges. Penalties under Ley 58/2003 (LGT) are tiered: 50% for minor negligence, 75% for serious negligent conduct, and 100%–150% of the undue VAT amount for deliberate or fraudulent claims (Art. 191 LGT). False invoicing or falsified export documentation attracts separate fines under Art. 201 LGT ranging from 50% to 200% of the transaction amount. Where deliberate under-declaration exceeds €150,000 (threshold raised by Organic Law 10/2023), criminal tax-fraud liability arises under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code, with imprisonment from one to five years, loss of subsidies, and disqualification. For MFO service exporters, AEAT specifically tests the reality of the foreign client's establishment, the economic substance of the cross-border arrangement, and the chain of payment; any recharacterisation of the place-of-supply as Spanish results in immediate denial of the 0% treatment with retroactive VAT assessment and penalty stacking.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign exchange and external transactions statistical oversight is also exercised jointly with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation (Secretaría General del Tesoro), while investment-services supervision for the MFO activity rests with the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Spain, as a Eurozone member, applies the consolidated EU capital-movement liberalization regime (Articles 63-66 TFEU). Both current-account and capital-account operations are freely convertible; no prior authorization or surrender obligations apply to non-residents' subscriptions, dividends, interest, or liquidation proceeds of an ES_SL. Residual statutory constraints are limited to (i) EU/UN sanctions and freezing measures, (ii) anti-money-laundering declaration thresholds, and (iii) balance-of-payments statistical returns. Profit remittances are unrestricted at the exchange-control level but must satisfy corporate law rules on distributable reserves (reduced capital, net worth floors) and, where applicable, 19% withholding tax on dividend distributions if the LAC/EU treaty rate does not reduce it. For portfolio-advisory clients, no foreign-exchange disadvantage arises as the company books income in EUR; euro/USD and euro/LATAM-currency exposures are managed through the hedging instruments enumerated below.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Spain imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender, repatriation deadline, or conversion ratio. All export and cross-border service receipts may be retained in foreign currency or freely converted. However, an ES_SL is subject to mandatory statistical declaration to Banco de España (Balance of Payments System, BOPS, via the SDO portal) for any transaction or aggregate of transactions with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000 within a calendar year, and to cash-physical-movement declaration (S-1/S-2 forms) for cross-border flows of banknotes/channels equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 under Law 10/2010. The MFO sector does not export goods; the same regime governs fee remittances from overseas family offices.

Operational Account and blocked Capital Escrow / equity commitment account (cuenta de depósito o bloqueada) for capital injections
Operational Account + custody account for a MiFID-licensed subsidiary; escrow sweep structures
Operational Account; low-cost treasury and international service desk for LATAM corridors
Operational Account; qualifying wealth-management onboarding for family-office principals

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility for the core treasury layer, Additional compliance scrutiny. Spanish-regulated EMIs/payment institutions (Licensed under Law 21/2011, Royal Decree 778/2023 and PSD2/Royal Decree-Law 19/2018) may lawfully provide client-facing payment accounts, SEPA and SWIFT pass-through services, and FX conversion. However, as the ES_SL is classified as a High_Risk_Special_License financial entity (ISIC 6430), most pan-EU EMIs (Revolut Business, Wise Business, Qonto, PASABank, Vivid) will decline onboarding or impose restrictive transaction caps pending CNMV license validation. Offshore EMIs (non-EU, no passport) cannot access TARGET2/SEPA and would require a correspondent credit institution, creating legal concentration risk and not satisfying the statutory 'account with a Spanish credit institution' expectations of the CNMV/AML supervisor. Viability: permissible only as a sub-threshold disbursement rail; not as a primary account or custody substitute.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person interview generally required for this risk tier. Law 10/2010 requires the identification of natural person signatories and UBOs; in practice, tier-1 Spanish banks will mandate a face-to-face (physical) compliance interview at the branch or in an official videoconference meeting with at least one appointed director and one UBO (or the manager of the family office acting under a notarized power of attorney). Remote opening (e.g., via video-identification) is legally permitted under the AML rulebook and is available at digital onboarding desks (Santander Línea Abierta, BBVA ABA), but the MFO's high-risk rating pushes the decision to the bank's GCO (Global Compliance Office), which consistently conditions the opening on an in-person meeting and sworn source-of-funds declaration. The notarized KYC deed (Acta notarial de identificación) and apostilled corporate excerpts reduce, but do not eliminate, the interview mandate; no Spanish bank will allow fully asynchronous onboarding for a discretionary portfolio-manager entity holding client money or authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Financial-sector classification (ISIC 6430) and discretionary authority over third-party family assets without full MiFID passported license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified CNMV registration certificate (EAFI/ESI or accepted MiFID exemption); investment management agreement template; compliance manual and conflicts-of-interest policy; written confirmation that the ES_SL does not hold client money or client securities (assets held with global custodians); regulator correspondence confirming the licensing path

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership opacity from LATAM multi-family trusts and foundations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deed/fideicomiso instrument; register of ultimate beneficial owners (owners of >25%); cascading organizational charts; notarized and apostilled UBO declarations; legal opinions from the origin jurisdiction verifying chain of title

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) among family office beneficiaries/principals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP-status declaration for each principal; independent PEP-database screening (World-Check/LexisNexis); source-of-wealth report (SOE) covering the last 5 years: tax returns, audited financial statements, professional background report, and the name of the regulator/auditor

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital contributions through offshore or non-cooperative jurisdictions (e.g., Panama, British Virgin Islands, UAE, or certain LATAM territories)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial rationale memo; tax-residence certificates (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal); CRS/FATCA registration attestation; insurance or trust holding documentation; correspondent bank references using KYC templates (SWIFT KYC Registry); traceability of funds from the origination date

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment orders and execution-only mandates that look like money laundering or tax evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed portfolio management agreement (contrato de gestión de carteras) with defined investment boundaries; explicit prohibition language on crypto/cash pass-through; target account registry delineating permissible custody beneficiaries; operational SOP with segregation of duties and dual control; audit trail of compliance sign-offs

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restrictive-measures name hits from a Spanish or EU consolidated list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal-name and alias documentation; passport/ID copies; date and place of birth; proof of non-convergence (e.g., transaction dates, jurisdictions, counterparties); negative screening reports and the rationale for false-positive determination; client file with screening timestamps

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity inconsistent with a dormant 'holding-like' MFO (law-suit or investment claims against the entity)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury and portfolio cash-flow forecast; custody reports showing the linkage of client money to separate funds; settlement calendar for debt issuance or real-asset closings; court or arbitration case reference if applicable, plus lawyer's confirmation letter

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of statutory corporate books (Libros obligatorios) in the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the province of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after closure of the financial year; for calendar-year companies, by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization triggers fines under Articles 38-39 of the Commercial Code and the Capital Companies Law; persistent failure impairs registration of subsequent corporate acts and may lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual financial statements (depósito de cuentas anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting approval within six months after financial year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year); filing with the Registry within one month after approval (by 31 July for calendar-year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within statutory deadline: fines up to EUR 60,000 under Article 283 of the Capital Companies Law; after repeated omission, closure of the company's registry sheet and final strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of ultimate beneficial ownership (titularidad real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil, embedded in the annual accounts deposit and AML files
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with each annual accounts filing (by 31 July for calendar-year); within 15 calendar days of any relevant ownership or control change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with Law 10/2010 on money laundering: fines from EUR 600 to EUR 60,000; registry restrictions and potential suspension of the EAFI/financial license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the expiration of the six-month period after the tax year close; calendar-year companies due by 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5 percent escalating to 20 percent plus late-payment interest; accuracy penalties; administrative tax seizure for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CNMV annual financial and activity filing for licensed multi-family office/EAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements and activity report within four months after financial year-end (by 30 April for calendar-year), subject to CNMV circulars on periodic reporting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under the Securities Market Act up to EUR 600,000 for serious breaches; possible license suspension and disqualification for directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all CNMV-registered financial advisory/EAFI entities irrespective of size; general SLs are subject to audit when at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: balance sheet total > EUR 2,850,000; net turnover > EUR 5,700,000; average headcount > 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) for individual statutory accounts; EU-adopted IFRS required for consolidated accounts when the group prepares them.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO information is confirmed annually as part of the deposit of annual accounts (Hoja de Titularidad Real). Any change in direct or indirect ownership or significant control must be recorded in the Registry of Members and declared to the Commercial Registry within 15 days; the register is open in electronic or physical form at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors or officers (if formally constituted; registration also made at the Commercial Registry)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Juntas Generales and, where applicable, of the Board)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per annum depending on registered office services and regulatory compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 8,000 per annum for a regulated EAFI/MFO-size SL requiring mandatory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period in which they obtain a positive tax base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created companies may apply the 15% rate described above. Other relevant incentives may include research and development deductions, technological innovation deductions, deductions for investment in qualifying audiovisual and other cultural productions, and participation-exemption treatment for qualifying dividends and capital gains. Spanish entities with net turnover below applicable statutory thresholds may qualify for reduced rates under transitional or small-enterprise provisions. Incentive availability must be tested annually against the effective legislation and anti-abuse rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. Spain does not impose a five-year expiry period for corporate tax losses. Utilization is generally subject to percentage limitations based on the taxpayer's net turnover and a minimum annual offset allowance of EUR 1 million, with special limitations for entities acquired after an ownership change and other anti-avoidance situations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, annual Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic office. Modelo 220 applies where the company is part of a Spanish consolidated tax group. Modelo 202 is used for advance corporate tax payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for Modelo 200; advance payments generally in April, October and December for Modelo 202.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the usual filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to the applicable annual calendar. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December, with electronic filing periods commonly extended to the first 20 calendar days of the relevant month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, Spanish tax identification number, registered address, tax period, entity type, filing type, activity classification, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not file this section for the Spanish SL. The Spanish SL must use its own Spanish NIF and identify its resident tax status. Foreign shareholders, branches, permanent establishments and group entities must be reported where the form requests related-party or participation information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax based on the approved statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish company's statutory accounting result. Do not substitute the foreign parent company's consolidated result. Intercompany transactions must be recorded consistently with the local books and supporting agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments converting accounting profit or loss into the Spanish tax result, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, exempt income, impairment adjustments, and other timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes, foreign exchange items, shareholder costs, non-arm's-length charges, and expenses lacking business purpose or documentation require separate Spanish tax analysis. Deductibility is not established solely by an invoice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning transactions with related parties, including transaction type, counterparty, amount, valuation method and applicable documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report dealings with foreign group companies, foreign controlling shareholders, common-control entities, financing vehicles, intellectual-property owners and service companies where Spanish related-party rules apply. Ensure consistency with the Local File, Master File and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available tax losses, losses used in the period, losses generated in the period and remaining balances, subject to statutory utilization limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign shareholder or foreign affiliate cannot be used by the Spanish SL merely because of common ownership. Verify ownership-change limitations and retain evidence supporting the historical tax-loss balances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments and loss utilization, followed by the applicable corporate tax rate, including any qualifying reduced rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the ordinary 25% rate unless the company demonstrably qualifies for a statutory reduced rate. A newly incorporated SL must verify that it is not a continuation of a previously conducted activity or controlled by a related entity in a manner excluding the 15% newly created-entity rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permitted deductions and credits, including qualifying R&D, technological innovation, cultural production and other statutory incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign incentives cannot be claimed on the Spanish return unless expressly recognized under Spanish law. Foreign taxes may require separate double-tax-relief analysis and cannot be deducted or credited twice for the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax withholdings, Modelo 202 advance payments and other payments on account available for offset against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding suffered by the Spanish SL is not automatically an advance payment of Spanish corporate tax. Apply treaty or domestic foreign-tax-credit rules only with supporting certificates and within statutory limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Final liability, refund or amount payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax payable after credits, withholdings and advance payments, including bank payment or refund details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent may fund the Spanish liability but should not be treated as the taxpayer. Refund claims should be supported by bank ownership, accounting records and evidence that the Spanish company bore the relevant tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover, balance-sheet and profit-and-loss data, related-party information, participation data, tax-loss schedules and other statistical disclosures required by the electronic return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Values must reconcile to the approved annual accounts, general ledger, VAT records, payroll records, withholding returns and transfer-pricing documentation. Foreign-currency amounts must be translated under applicable Spanish accounting and tax rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty of EUR 100, reduced by 50% for voluntary filing without prior notice where the statutory conditions are met. Late filing with tax payable generally attracts a surcharge of 1% of the unpaid amount for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, with no separate daily surcharge; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest for the excess period. The surcharge may be reduced by 25% if statutory payment and filing conditions are satisfied. Understatement, omitted income, false deductions or fraudulent conduct may trigger tax penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid tax, plus interest and collection measures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish resident company to non-resident shareholders, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may eliminate withholding where the statutory minimum participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form and anti-abuse requirements are satisfied. Domestic participation-exemption rules may also apply to qualifying corporate recipients, but they do not automatically remove the payer's withholding obligation without the required exemption conditions and evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain valid evidence of the recipient's tax residence, beneficial ownership and entitlement to treaty or directive relief. A current tax residence certificate from the foreign tax authority should be retained, together with ownership records, holding-period evidence, legal-form and subject-to-tax evidence, recipient declarations, beneficial-owner analysis and anti-abuse support. Apply the reduced rate only where Spanish procedural requirements permit source relief; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue any available refund through the AEAT procedure. File the relevant Spanish withholding return, generally Modelo 216, and annual information return, generally Modelo 296, within their applicable deadlines. Treaty relief is unavailable for conduit arrangements, artificial structures, beneficial-ownership failures or arrangements principally designed to obtain an improper tax benefit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic non-resident income tax withholding is generally 24% on Spanish-source royalties and interest paid to non-residents, reduced to 19% for qualifying recipients resident in the EU or in the European Economic Area where the applicable statutory conditions are met. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty and interest rates, frequently to rates in the 0% to 10% range, but the exact rate depends on the treaty, recipient residence, beneficial ownership and applicable limitations. Interest and royalty payments qualifying under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may be exempt where the associated-company ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions are met. Spanish-source characterization, permanent-establishment exposure, treaty entitlement and beneficial ownership must be documented before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The principal Master File threshold is generally a consolidated group net turnover of at least EUR 45 million. A Spanish Local File is generally required for material related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions, including the aggregate EUR 250,000 threshold for transactions of the same type with the same related person or entity during the tax period. The EUR 250,000 threshold does not eliminate documentation requirements for transactions subject to special rules, transactions involving tax havens, or transactions otherwise covered by specific statutory provisions. Certain low-value or routine transactions may qualify for simplified documentation. The documentation must be available by the tax-return filing deadline and supplied to the AEAT upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Economic substance is nevertheless enforced through Spanish transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, the general anti-abuse rule, the anti-elusion rule, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse standards, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, interest-limitation rules and anti-tax-haven provisions. A multi-family office must demonstrate genuine Spanish functions, qualified personnel, decision-making capacity, risk control, premises or operational infrastructure proportionate to its activity, regulated authorization where required, and commercially supportable remuneration. A Spanish SL that merely invoices advisory fees while investment decisions, client control, custody, personnel and risks remain abroad faces recharacterization, denial of deductions, withholding disputes and possible permanent-establishment or regulatory findings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed investment services and financial-regulatory breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing discretionary portfolio management, investment advice, reception or transmission of orders, dealing, custody or other regulated investment services without the required authorization, registration or passporting arrangement. A multi-family office must distinguish non-regulated family-office coordination from regulated services under Spanish securities legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions under Spanish securities legislation may include public or private reprimands, substantial monetary fines, suspension or limitation of authorization, removal of managers and prohibition from conducting regulated activities. Unauthorized activity may also generate client restitution, contract disputes and referral to criminal authorities where fraud or other offenses are present.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur administrative, civil and, where intentional fraud or unlawful solicitation is involved, criminal liability. Personal exposure can include restitution, asset preservation, management disqualification and imprisonment where a separate criminal offense is proven. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require judicial or statutory authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing advisory or management income, fabricating expenses, using sham service companies, misclassifying dividends as deductible interest, manipulating transfer prices, or claiming deductions without a genuine business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, fraudulent means and severity, in addition to tax, late-payment interest and collection costs. Criminal tax fraud generally requires a tax loss exceeding EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax period. Basic criminal tax fraud may carry imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded, together with professional or public-office disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable for tax debts where statutory management-liability conditions are met, particularly after failure to pay, repeated non-compliance or dissolution without proper settlement. Criminal liability requires personal participation, intent or legally relevant omission. Courts may order asset seizure, civil restitution and restrictions on leaving Spain; imprisonment is not a routine consequence of an ordinary filing error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees, royalties or interest to foreign affiliates; shifting Spanish profits through non-arm's-length arrangements; failing to prepare required Local File or Master File; or reporting amounts inconsistent with the functional profile and actual conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment to the arm's-length result, impose a corresponding adjustment where legally available, deny deductions, recalculate withholding and impose documentation penalties. Documentation-related penalties may be calculated by reference to undisclosed or incorrectly disclosed amounts, subject to statutory limits; general tax penalties may apply where the adjustment produces unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face corporate civil liability for losses caused by deliberate or grossly negligent transfer-pricing conduct and may become tax-liable under statutory secondary-liability rules. Criminal exposure arises only where the facts satisfy the separate elements and thresholds of tax fraud, accounting falsification, insolvency offenses or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, terrorist financing and AML-control failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained client wealth, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring politically exposed person risks, processing unusual custody wires, failing to report suspicious activity, or maintaining inadequate customer due diligence and recordkeeping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may result in significant fines, public or private reprimands, temporary or permanent restrictions on activities, management disqualification and other supervisory measures. For entities, statutory maximum fines may reach the higher applicable amount based on the breach, including millions of euros or a percentage of annual turnover or net worth, depending on the classification and current statutory limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The compliance officer, board members and responsible managers may be sanctioned personally where the breach is attributable to them. The company may face account freezes, transaction restrictions, loss of banking access and license consequences. Criminal money-laundering liability may carry imprisonment, fines, confiscation and judicial asset-securing measures; travel bans require judicial order and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominees, undisclosed fiduciaries, circular ownership, opaque foundations, back-to-back entities or false declarations to conceal the controlling person or the ultimate source or destination of client assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include AML sanctions, refusal or restriction of banking and custody services, tax recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, beneficial-owner registry issues, confiscation proceedings and penalties for false corporate or tax information. Fraudulent documentation may create separate criminal offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto controllers may face civil restitution, disqualification, administrative penalties and criminal liability for fraud, document offenses or money laundering. Corporate limited liability does not protect persons who personally participated in concealment or abuse of the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit extraction and disguised distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying personal expenses of shareholders or directors, making undocumented shareholder loans, declaring dividends without distributable profits, paying excessive related-party remuneration, or disguising distributions as royalties, interest or consultancy charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payment may be reclassified as a dividend, remuneration or constructive distribution, with corporate tax adjustments, withholding tax, late-payment interest and penalties. Improper distributions may also violate Spanish company-law capital-maintenance rules and require repayment to the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for unlawful distributions and for company losses caused by breach of fiduciary and corporate-law duties. Shareholders who knowingly received unlawful distributions may owe restitution. Serious concealment or asset diversion may lead to insolvency, fraud or accounting-crime proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, falsifying client-asset records, recording fictitious receivables, destroying accounting evidence, preferentially paying insiders while insolvent, or continuing operations while knowingly unable to meet obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible consequences include tax reassessment, accounting sanctions, civil damages, insolvency disqualification, clawback of transactions, creditor restitution and criminal penalties for falsification, fraud or insolvency offenses. Client assets held in custody may be subject to segregation, tracing and recovery proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the insolvency deficit where the insolvency is culpable and may face asset seizure, disqualification from administration of third-party assets, civil restitution and imprisonment where the conduct constitutes a criminal offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False residence, treaty-shopping and withholding-tax abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming treaty or EU directive relief without valid tax residence, beneficial ownership, subject-to-tax status or holding-period evidence; routing dividends, interest or royalties through conduit entities; or creating artificial arrangements to obtain reduced withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be required to pay the under-withheld tax, interest and penalties. The recipient may lose treaty relief, face reassessment in its residence jurisdiction and become subject to anti-abuse or beneficial-ownership challenges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize false certificates, sham arrangements or deliberate under-withholding may face corporate civil liability, tax-liability derivation and criminal exposure for tax fraud, document falsification or money laundering where the statutory elements are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Data, confidentiality and client-asset control failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disclosing confidential family-office information without lawful basis, commingling client assets with company funds, transferring assets without authorization, or failing to maintain adequate cybersecurity and access controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include data-protection fines, regulatory sanctions, civil damages, restitution, contract termination, banking restrictions and, where assets are misappropriated, criminal investigation and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face civil liability for inadequate supervision and personal criminal liability for intentional misuse, unauthorized disclosure or misappropriation. Travel bans and imprisonment require judicial proceedings and are not automatic corporate-law penalties.
